If area >40% of image, multiply its area_norm by 0.8 (not 0.5) before computing Salience; if a large-area candidate has detector_confidence ≥0.60 or substantially higher local_contrast, allow it to remain competitive (foreground rescue).
- Choose the subject with highest salience. If two candidates are within 5% salience, prefer the one that yields more distinct high‑signal tokens early (color, multiword class, accessory, number, or short OCR token).

Placement and high‑signal token rules (deterministic)
- First content token must be a high‑signal token (color/multiword class/number/text) unless impossible. Require at least one high‑signal token within the first 2 content words. Allow exactly one deterministic exception only if grammaticality is impossible; in that case the token must be within the first 4 content words.
- If two distinct high‑signal tokens are clearly visible, require both within the first 4 content words unless that makes the sentence ungrammatical; otherwise place one before the verb and the other immediately after it.
- Do not precede the first high‑signal token with verbs or extraneous function words (omit or drop the leading article if it delays high‑signal tokens).
- When a visible numeral/count meets visibility rules, use an Arabic numeral and place it early (within first 2–4 content words).

Class, wording and modifier constraints
- Start with a concise noun phrase: prefer [Color/Number/Multword‑class] + [class]. Prefer multiword concrete classes when available.
- Use present‑tense, concise S + V (+ O) sentences and common collocations ("X holds Y", "X sits on Y", "X leans against Y").
- Limit modifiers: at most one pre‑nominal adjective (color/pattern/accessory) and at most one short post‑nominal prepositional phrase or one compact participial phrase. Allow one compact extra descriptor overall. Avoid subordinate clauses and stacked prepositional phrases.
- Aim for noun‑dense captions with concrete tokens early; minimize function words that delay concrete tokens.

OCR/token formatting notes
- Prefer direct inclusion of short OCR tokens (e.g., shirt NIKE, sign STOP) without extra wrapper words when OCR rules are met. If quotes are required for clarity, keep them minimal; avoid verbose wrappers like "sign reading" unless necessary for grammar. Do not copy phone numbers or long digit sequences.

Templates and micro‑patterns (use these as patterns, not literal fill)
- [Color] [multiword_class] [verb] [object] → "Red double-decker bus passes street."
- [Numeral] [multiword_class] [verb] [modifier] → "3 yellow school buses stop at corner."
- [multiword_class] [OCR_TEXT] [verb] [object] → "Shirt NIKE worn by young man."

Examples (follow these styles; do not output these examples)
- Good: "Young woman in red coat holds black umbrella."
- Good: "White stop sign beside brick building."

- Bad: "Man leans on sign with 212-625-9212 printed." (do not copy phone numbers / low‑confidence OCR)

Deterministic tie‑breakers and limits
- When subjects tie, prefer the subject that yields more distinct high‑signal tokens early.
- Limit caption length to 8–14 total words. Aim for ~9–12 content words when possible.
- Enforce the visibility/OCR thresholds strictly. Do not invent unseen attributes or guess unreadable text.
